warmup.text: The Lady Wilma is heading south toward the bottom of South America. Today there is a pig, a cook with a cleaver, and a hard question for Jack. Before you read, think about what you would do if someone offered you a ticket home.

words.text: This week's roots are rid and ris, which mean laugh, and lud and lus, which mean play. In the game, sail through the narrows. Pick the channel with the word that really carries the root.

reading.text: Read Chapter 4. Notice who the joke is on as the pig hunt grows. Then watch the chapter turn serious in the harbor at Rio. Listen to how Jack sounds when the jokes stop.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 4. Then plan your adventure scene: who is there, where it happens, what goes wrong, and one line your hero says. Start in the middle of the action.

glossary.meaning: a private bedroom on a ship
the attitude a writer takes toward what is happening

rid: This word is about laughing at someone.
It is the laugh root that ends in d.
lud: This word is about a game or a joke.
It is the play root that ends in d.
ris: This word is about mocking laughter.
It is the laugh root that ends in s.
lus: This word is about a trick on your eyes.
It is the play root that ends in s.
lude: A playful pause between two acts.
The play root, plus a silent e.

miss.whispered: Whispered tells how loud: very quietly.
miss.bellowed: Bellowed tells how loud: a huge, deep shout.
miss.pleaded: Pleaded tells a feeling: someone begging.
miss.grumbled: Grumbled tells a feeling: someone cross and complaining.
miss.replied: Replied only tells that someone answered.

game.title: Through the Strait
game.sub: This week's word game · 6 narrows today
game.look: The Strait of Magellan is a narrow, twisting passage of water at the bottom of South America. Here your ship works west through it, from the Atlantic to the Pacific. At each narrows, read the clue and pick the safe channel: the word that really fits. Every narrows you pass lights a fire on the shore of Tierra del Fuego, the Land of Fire.

do: Read the clue at the narrows.
Look at the word in each channel.
Tap the channel with the word that really fits.
Tap Sail on.
how.why: A root only helps if it is really there, and a speech spelling only works if the apostrophe is in the right place.

game.doneLine: The Pacific is open. Come back tomorrow for six more narrows.

narrows.clue: Find the word with lud (play): to slip away from someone, as if in a game of tag.
narrows.why: e (out) + lud (play): to play your way out. Include comes from clud, which means close.
de (down) + rid (laugh): to laugh down at someone. A riddle is a puzzle; it only looks like it has the root.
narrows.miss: Is a riddle about laughing at someone? Look at the other channel.

narrows.clue: Find the word with lus (play): a secret trick that two people play together.
narrows.why: col (together) + lus (play). Conclusion comes from clud, which means close.

narrows.clue: Find the word with ris (laugh): laughter that mocks someone.
narrows.why: de + ris + ion: mocking laughter. Decision comes from cis, which means cut.

narrows.clue: Chapter 1: a cold passenger shouts that someone has been hogging the stove. Which spelling shows how he says it?
narrows.why: hoggin' = hogging. The apostrophe sits where the g is missing, at the end.

narrows.clue: Chapter 1: Captain Swain roars at the stowaways for inviting in the weather. Which spelling is his?
narrows.why: invitin' = inviting. A missing letter needs an apostrophe in its place.
narrows.miss: A letter is missing. What marks the spot?

virtue.name: self-control
virtue.title: Self-control or not?
virtue.intro: This week's virtue is self-control: staying calm and choosing what you do, even when you feel scared, angry or excited. Sort these everyday examples.

items.t: You feel nervous before a test, so you take a slow breath and start with the first question.
items.why: You notice the feeling and choose a calm next step.

items.t: Your little brother knocks over your tower, and you yell and knock over his.
items.why: The anger is choosing for you. Self-control means you choose.

items.t: You want to blurt out the answer, but you wait for your turn.
items.why: You hold back what you feel like doing because waiting is right.

items.t: A friend wins the game, and you say good game even though you feel let down.
items.why: You keep your disappointment from hurting someone else.

art.title: Bay of Rio de Janeiro
art.alt: A watercolor of a wide harbor: a sailing ship under full sail with cannon smoke beside it, another ship at anchor, small boats, and a tall rounded mountain on the right.
art.look: A French artist painted the bay of Rio de Janeiro in 1837, twelve years before the novel. Cannon smoke drifts across the water as a ship sails in, and Sugarloaf Mountain rises on the right. In Chapter 4 the Lady Wilma also passes under the fortress guns of Rio de Janeiro.
